- **self**: Metaphor collision as a detection signal (3/2)

## How it works

- [statement] MIPVU labels a word metaphor-related when its contextual meaning contrasts with a more basic meaning and can be understood by comparison with it. It is a per-lexical-unit procedure; two colliding domains would be found only by labelling each word separately and then comparing their source domains. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10666762/ · keywords: Metaphor collision as a detection signal · also: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2212.08395
- [statement] Incongruity-based metaphor detection is invalid for conventional metaphors, because the surrounding context is usual for the target word. A collision signal is therefore strongest for novel or freshly chosen figures and weak for dead ones. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/pdf/2212.08395 · keywords: Metaphor collision as a detection signal · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.15357v1

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Cross-dataset evaluation finds LLM metaphor detection tracks lexical overlap and sentence length, and accuracy on literal paraphrases often drops or paraphrases keep the metaphor. An LLM-based collision detector should not be trusted without a check against a source-domain lexicon. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-07-21) — https://arxiv.org/html/2507.15357v1 · keywords: Metaphor collision as a detection signal
